subject: Aligning SLA tags with per-route cost hooks - ACME spike follow-up
messages:
From: Terry Harrington <ops@acme.example.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 18 Jul 2027 08:42:00 -0700
Subject: Sudden route cost spike and SLA tagging question

Hi Aditya,

We saw a sharp cost spike across a handful of our routes this morning (attached CSV with samples). The spike correlates with a set of high-concurrency chat endpoints that we tag as 'interactive'. Our billing shows these under a lumped project code and it's hard to map back to route-level SLA ownership.

Quick asks:
- Can Redwood provide a route-level tag that we can use in our billing exports? Ideally the tag flows through to the per-tenant cost CSV.
- Is there a way to mark a route as SLA-critical so it surfaces in the console with different sampling and alert thresholds?

This is hitting our SLOs and we'd like to avoid broad throttles that impact other workloads. I've attached a short sample (acme_spike_log.csv) and one screenshot of the cost view. Happy to jump on a quick call if useful.

Thanks,
Terry Harrington
Platform Ops, ACME Data

Attachments: acme_spike_log.csv, route_cost_sample.png
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Terry Harrington <ops@acme.example.com>
Date: Sun, 18 Jul 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Sudden route cost spike and SLA tagging question

Folks,

Forwarding ACME's note — they hit a cost spike and need clearer per-route attribution + a way to mark SLA-critical routes in the Console so sampling/alerts are different. Key asks: route-level billing tag and per-route SLA flag that affects sampling/alerting.

Sooj, is this something we can satisfy with existing 'route metadata' fields and a console toggle? Marissa/Ben — if we need infra/observability work, can you scope the minimum MVP: a boolean SLA tag on route config that surfaces in the console and the billing export, plus a lightweight change to sampling rules?

Proposed quick scope (MVP):
- Add a route config field: sla_priority: [default|critical] (defaults to default)
- Export sla_priority in daily billing CSV and per-tenant route breakdowns
- Console: per-route detail shows sla_priority and a link to 'adjust sampling/alert profile' (UX work minimal)
- Immediate interim: provide a one-off mapping file or dashboard for ACME while we ship the config change

Ping me with estimates and blockers. ACME is open to a short patch/fix while we formalize.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Product Manager, Console & Observability
Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Terry Harrington <ops@acme.example.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2027 09:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Sudden route cost spike and SLA tagging question

Thanks for the ping — this seems straightforward but there are a few nuances:

1) Billing pipeline: We already emit route_id in internal exports, but the downstream billing join currently uses project/service tags only. We can add sla_priority as a column before the final join; low complexity but needs a migration window.

2) Sampling/alerts: Our sampling system supports per-route overrides; exposing a console toggle to flip to a 'critical profile' is mostly UI + API wiring. The real work is the alert threshold templates for critical routes (we should define templates).

3) Backfill & edge cases: For routes that are proxied or have dynamic route resolution, we need guardrails so sla_priority isn't lost.

Estimated effort (MVP):
- Backend (billing export column + safe migrate): 3 dev-days (Marissa + infra help)
- API + sampling wiring: 2 dev-days (Ben/observability)
- Console UI: 3 frontend-days (Sooj)
- Docs + rollout plan: 1 day

If we can prioritize this in the next sprint I can get a short-lived dashboard for ACME in ~48 hours (ad-hoc query) while the product change ships.

I'll open OBS-1247 with the proposed tasks and keep ACME in the loop.

-Ben
Ben Carter
Engineering Manager, Observability
Redwood Inference
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Terry Harrington <ops@acme.example.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Jul 2027 16:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Sudden route cost spike and SLA tagging question

All,

Thanks — I like the MVP scope. Quick clarifications before we commit to sprint:

- UX: The console change will be a small per-route switch with a confirmation modal. We'll also add an indicator in the route list (colored dot) so critical routes are visible at a glance.
- Policy: Need to confirm whether only org owners can flip SLA priority or project admins — Irene, can you advise on the permission model?
- Templates: Ben, can you draft two alert templates (latency-critical, cost-spike) we can wire to the sampling profiles? I can mock the UI around them.

If no objections, I'll add the UI task to the sprint and Ben/Marissa can pick the backend tickets. Aditya — can you own communication to ACME and share the ad-hoc dashboard link when ready?

Irene, one more ask: for ACME's temporary mapping dashboard, can Customer Success confirm who in their org should get direct access and whether they want daily automated exports during the rollout?

I'll attach a short drive doc with the mock and the proposed permission table (link in metadata).

— Soojin
SoojIN Lee
Product Manager, Console UX
Redwood Inference
